- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7–10 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 7–10 days) and underestimates late (last 10–15 days); apply asymmetric correction: +1% for first 7 days, -1% for last 10 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
